results.title: What Makes You So Smart, Computational Neuroscientist? - Pacific Standard
results.content: Terrence Sejnowski always knew he was the “science nerd,” but it was a stint with his high school’s radio club that sent him on a path that would lead him to becoming a pioneer in computational neuroscience. The Francis Crick professor at the Salk Institute and the director of the Crick-Jacobs Center for Theoretical and Computational Biology talked to *Pacific Standard* about searching for Sputnik, the problem with schooling, and receiving pleasure reading material from a Nobel Prize winner. He had a master’s degree in physics and, more than the other teachers, he was a hands-on type of guy who liked to have big projects. **You knew that you were a “science nerd,” but did you think of yourself as very smart? I did very well in terms of exams and contests, but what I really learned in high school was that that wasn’t really the goal. In the radio club, we would ask ourselves, “What is your mission?” When you’re in high school and you ask that, it makes you think twice about how to achieve it.
